q: A table contains one row per medication order. What is its grain?
why: Grain is the real-world unit represented by one row: a medication-order record.

q: Which is the strongest first step when asked to 'analyze hypertension patients'?
options: Clarify the decision, population, outcome, setting and period
why: A valid analysis starts with an answerable question and explicit definitions.

q: A number used to code ward categories 1, 2 and 3 is usually:
why: Numeric labels do not make categories quantitative.

q: A variable associated with both treatment selection and outcome may distort their observed relationship. It is called:
why: Confounding can distort an exposure-outcome association and requires design-aware handling.

q: Why should the unit of analysis be specified?
options: It prevents confusing counts of patients, encounters and orders
why: Different units produce different counts and require different statistical assumptions.
